To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) C3 photosynthetic activity predominates in Clusia minor leaves during the wet and dry season, although CAM is induced during the dry season, (2) the contribution from PEPcarboxylase to CO2 assimilation is greater in Clusia leaves during the wet than the dry season, and (3) the down-regulation of PEPcarboxylation during phase II occurs more slowly in Clusia than has been reported for other CAM plants.

(a) C3 photosynthetic metabolism predominates over the C3-C4 intermediate Clusia during the wet season, (b) CAM activity is induced during the dry season, but C4 carboxylase continues to operate during phase II of the diurnal cycle, and (c) the carbon-isotope discrimination ratio of leaf organic material is not a good indicator of the relative importance of the C3 and C4 pathways in Clusia minor.

(1) the down regulation of phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase (PEPc) in Clusia minor is slower than has been suggested by laboratory studies, and (2) the contribution of C4 carboxylase to daytime CO2 uptake during the dry season may be greater than has previously been assumed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physiological and molecular basis of the transition from C-3 to C-4 photosynthesis in the C-3-C-4 intermediate Clusia.
the study of the physiology, biochemistry and molecular biology of the C3–C4 intermediate Clusia.
the physiological and molecular aspects of the C3–C4 intermediate Clusia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
C3 photosynthesis dominates CO2 uptake by Clusia minor during the wet season, but during the dry season, C4 carboxylating activity predominates in leaves of this species.

the carbon isotope ratios measured in the leaf organic matter of Clusia minor are not simply an integrated measure of the instantaneous carbon isotope ratios of the CO2 assimilated during photosynthesis.

the carbon isotope discrimination values measured in the leaves of C. minor were consistent with a mixture of photosynthetic pathways, but the extent of the contribution of CAM to the overall carbon isotope discrimination in this plant is still unclear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CAM in C3-CAM intermediates is not a simple switch between two different photosynthetic mechanisms but rather a continuum of photosynthetic behaviour which is determined by the environmental conditions and by the physiological state of the plant.
the C3-C4 intermediate Clusia is able to switch between C3 and CAM modes of CO2 fixation to maximize photosynthesis under different environmental conditions.
the contribution of CAM to the overall carbon budget of Clusia is relatively small and that the carbon isotopic composition of Clusia organic matter is dominated by C3 carboxylations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the C3-C4 intermediate Clusia has a remarkable ability to switch rapidly between the two photosynthetic pathways and that the contribution from each pathway to total carbon fixation varies considerably throughout the day and over the annual cycle.
the C3 pathway is the main pathway in Clusia minor, and CAM is used as a supplemental pathway.
the carbon isotope ratio of Clusia minor leaves was not affected by the transition between CAM and C3 photosynthesis.
